headline: Celtics choke away a three-one lead and get bounced at the Garden
morning_brew: The Celtics just turned a dream season into a complete nightmare at the Garden. Losing 109-100 in a Game 7 after being up 3-1 in the series is absolutely brutal. Philadelphia became the fourteenth team in history to pull that off, and they did it right on our floor. Jaylen Brown had thirty-three points, but it was not enough to stop the bleeding. We have eighteen banners hanging above us, but this group forgot how to close out a series when it mattered most.

Over at Fenway Park, the Red Sox are still stuck in a massive rut after a 6-3 loss to the Astros. The starter Early struggled on the mound, lasting only four innings and giving up five earned runs. We are sitting at 13-20 now, which is a sub-.400 winning percentage that makes every Dunks run taste a little more bitter. Wilyer Abreu had two hits and an RBI, but the pitching just cannot keep us in these games. It is a long summer ahead if they do not find some consistency soon.

The news does not get much better for the rest of the Hub. Charlie McAvoy is facing an in-person hearing for that slash, which could mean a long suspension to start next season. It is another headache for a team that already had a disappointing exit. Meanwhile, the Patriots are grinding through OTAs and making decisions on fifth-year options for the 2023 class. Fourteen wins last season set a high bar, and the front office has to decide who actually fits into the long-term plan in Foxborough.

news_digest.headline: 76ers, Embiid vanquish Celtics to complete 3-1 comeback
news_digest.dans_take: A total collapse that is going to haunt this city for a long time.
